thread:
Maya Chen: @here VanguardX wants to run a POC importing their fin-docs index + chat. They want to use orchid-70b-quant (q4_0) variant. Asking for throughput 300 rps, sub-200ms p50 gen latency, and enterprise KMS/HSM. Also sent a security questionnaire they want answered before kickoff.

Alex Ramos: OK — thanks. Timeline: they want POC in 2 weeks. Pricing ask: committed qps pricing? will we offer burst capacity? :thinking:

Devon Patel: Dev note: orchid-70b-quant uses grouped quant kernels; KV cache is memory heavy. On 8xA100 80GB pool we'll hit ~1.1GB KV per convo at 2k seq. Need to validate batch size. Also tokenizer mismatch — their data uses custom tokens.

Maya Chen: @Devon can we serve a pinned variant or fallback to orchid-70b-fp16? Customer insists on quant for cost.

Devon Patel: We can expose orchid-70b-q4a (our q4 variant) but we haven't validated tokenization behavior vs upstream orchid tokenizer. Risk: hallucination delta. Also HSM integration: Private requires KMS+HSM config, will add ~3 days infra work.

Priya Singh: Security: their questionnaire wants encryption in transit+at rest, HSM-backed keys, SOC2 attestation, and customer audit logging. Private deployment will satisfy most, but confirm egress rules for customer data.

Alex Ramos: Pricing: propose committed reserved capacity for 3 months at 20% discount plus overage at hosted rates. Are there unit cost numbers for q4 variants?

Devon Patel: Rough per-token estimate: hosted q4 variant ~0.0012 USD per 1k tokens (model-only), but dedicated infra unit economics depend on batch/kv hit. I'll run a microbenchmark and share numbers in ~24h.

Maya Chen: Action items: 1) Devon run benchmark on orchid-70b-q4a (tokenization + kv/mem) 2) Priya to map questionnaire blockers 3) Alex to send draft pricing and reserve ask 4) assign POC engineer.

Devon Patel: I'll post results here. Starting run now:
```bash
# run on perf-lab
python perf/run_perf.py --model orchid-70b-q4a --seq 2048 --batch 4 --kv-cache
```

deploy-bot: perf job 6843210123 started by Devon Patel

Maya Chen: @Priya can you take lead on the legal/security q? I can loop in the customer for clarifications tomorrow.

Priya Singh: Yep — I'll triage the questionnaire and flag anything that needs legal. Quick q: do we have an HSM partner checklist I can reuse?

Devon Patel: Ping me if you need a memory breakdown table; I'll include the perf artifact and sample tokens.

Alex Ramos: I'll draft pricing and a short SOW for reserved capacity. Also FYI customer asked if we support canary rollouts between fp16 and q4 — answer: yes via rollout config, but we should warn about quality deltas.

Maya Chen: Thanks team. If perf looks good, we'll propose dedicated pilot + security review next week. :thumbsup:

Devon Patel: Perf results: p50 gen 180ms, p95 420ms at 300 rps simulated with batching=2. KV memory per session ~1.05GB. Tokenizer mismatch: ~3% tokenization delta vs customer tokenizer, might need a preprocessing step. Uploading logs: https://redwood.internal/perf/6843210123

Priya Singh: Reviewed questionnaire — main blockers: HSM proof, data residency, audit log retention. Suggested mitigations attached. I'll schedule ops meeting with customer.

Alex Ramos: Great. I'll send the pricing proposal and SOW later today.

Maya Chen: Closing loop — next steps owned. Thanks all.
